questions.question: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. Together they finish in (days)
A takes 10 days and B takes 15 days to do a job. The ratio of their efficiencies A : B is
questions.explanation: Efficiency is inversely proportional to time: 15 : 10 = 3 : 2.

questions.question: If A is twice as efficient as B and B alone takes 24 days, A alone takes (days)
questions.explanation: A takes half the time: 12 days.

questions.question: 12 men can do a job in 10 days. 15 men can do it in (days)
A job takes 8 men 9 days. If 6 men work, they take (days)
If A is 25% more efficient than B and B takes 20 days, A takes (days)
questions.explanation: The efficiency ratio is 5 : 4, so the times are 4 : 5. A = 20 × 4/5 = 16.

questions.question: 6 men working 9 hours a day complete a job in 10 days. 9 men working 5 hours a day will take (days)
20 workers can finish a job in 30 days. After 10 days, 5 workers leave. The remaining workers need how many more days? (to one decimal place)
A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. A starts, and after 5 days B joins. The total time is (days)
questions.explanation: A does 1/4 in 5 days. The remaining 3/4 at 1/12 per day takes 9 days. Total 14.

questions.question: A can do a job in 12 days, B in 15 days. They work together for 3 days, and A leaves. B finishes the rest alone in (days)
questions.explanation: In 3 days they do 3 × 9/60 = 27/60. Left 33/60; B does 4/60 per day, so 8.25 days.

questions.question: A is thrice as efficient as B. Together they finish a job in 18 days. A alone takes (days)
questions.explanation: Rates 3x and x: 4x = 1/18, so A = 3/72 = 1/24. A takes 24 days.

questions.question: 15 men finish a job in 20 days. How many men will finish it in 12 days?
A worker's efficiency rises by 20%. He earlier took 30 days for a job. He now takes (days)
4 men and 6 women can finish a job in 8 days; 3 men and 7 women can finish it in 10 days. The ratio of the efficiency of a man to that of a woman is
A and B can finish a job in 12 and 18 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. A finishes the rest in (days)
questions.explanation: In 4 days they do 4 × 5/36 = 5/9. Left 4/9 at A's rate 1/12: 16/3 = 5.33 days.

questions.question: A can do a job in 10 days. B is 25% less efficient than A. They work together for 4 days. The fraction of the job left is
questions.explanation: B's rate = 0.75 × 1/10 = 3/40. Together 7/40 per day. In 4 days 28/40 = 7/10 is done, so 3/10 is left.

questions.question: Efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. A alone takes 30 days. All three together take (days)
questions.explanation: Rates 2, 3, 5 units; A's 2 units take 30 days so total job = 60 units. Together 10 units a day: 6 days.

questions.question: 20 men were to finish a job in 40 days. After 10 days, 10 more men joined. The job finished in how many days from the start?
questions.explanation: Total 800 man-days. After 10 days 600 remain. 30 men take 20 days. Total 30.

questions.question: A takes 24 days and B takes 36 days to do a job. They work on alternate days, starting with A. The job is finished in (days)
questions.explanation: A + B pair does 1/24 + 1/36 = 5/72 per two days. After 28 days (14 pairs) 70/72 is done. A then does 3/72 on day 29, completing the job.

questions.question: A and B together finish a job in 6 days. A alone takes 5 days less than B alone. A alone takes (days)
questions.explanation: Let A = x and B = x + 5. 1/x + 1/(x + 5) = 1/6 gives x² − 7x − 30 = 0, so x = 10.
